title: i made an 8-legged spider for my game using ai and gave it full locomotion
author: Delicious-Shower8401
selftext:
At this point, generating a humanoid character, rigging it and throwing some animations on top isn't really that **surprising anymore**.

So I wanted to try something less straightforward.

**I made this eight-legged spider creature for my game and pushed the workflow all the way from a single concept to a game-ready animated character with proper locomotion.**

The workflow was roughly:

* generated the initial creature concept in **Lychee Studio AI**
* separated it into individual parts instead of trying to generate the whole thing as one mesh
* generated several additional parts with Tripo P2
* assembled and cleaned everything up in **Blender**
* retopologized and baked the heavier meshes
* created a custom rig for all eight legs
* built the locomotion and procedural leg movement so the feet react properly to the ground

**Lychee Studio AI** has probably been the most useful tool for this kind of workflow so far. It’s node-based, so I can handle image generation, 3D generation, texturing, cleanup and the rest of the pipeline in one place instead of constantly jumping between different tools. Image generation is especially convenient there because it’s quick to iterate, and having multiple 3D generators in the same workflow makes the whole process much easier to manage.

And surprisingly, it does.

There is still plenty of manual work involved, especially around rigging, weights and locomotion, but this feels much closer to an actual game-production workflow than just generating a static 3D model.
